 Lyon, Brussels, and Almaty previews and predictions  
 October 20, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Tournament previews 
 9 
 The Asian swing came to an end with yet another surprising result at the Shanghai Masters , as Alejandro Davidovich Fokina defeated fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final. Now the home stretch of the tennis season really begins on European indoor hard courts. ATP 250s in Lyon, Brussels, and Almaty take place this week. Among those in action are Daniil Medvedev, Alexander Bublik, Andrey Rublev, Stefanos Tsitsipas, Arthur Fils, Flavio Cobolli, and Taylor Fritz.
 Let’s break down the three tournaments.    
 Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes 
 Where : Lyon, France  
 Surface : Indoor hard  
 Prize money : 757,320 Euros  
 Points : 250  
 Top seed : Flavio Cobolli 
 Defending champion : Ugo Humbert
 Draw analysis : Just about anything could happen in Lyon, as the seeded players are hardly reliable right now and the unseeded contingent is strong. Parity looks like the overriding theme of this 28-man field. Cobolli is struggling, Fritz and Lorenzo Musetti have battled through injury-plagued 2026 campaigns, and Brandon Nakashima may have run out of gas at the end of a long year. Unseeded floaters to keep an eye on include Matteo Berrettini, Martin Landaluce, and Benjamin Bonzi. Stan Wawrinka is also in the draw, playing the penultimate tournament of his career. Meanwhile, an indoor hard court at home in France could be just what the doctor ordered for defending champion Ugo Humbert.
 Hot : Arthur Fery, Titouan Droguet
 Cold : Flavio Cobolli, Lorenzo Musetti, Ugo Humbert, Matteo Berrettini, Stan Wawrinka
 Quarterfinal predictions : Matteo Berrettini over Martin Landaluce, Valentin Vacherot over Lorenzo Sonego, Ugo Humbert over Tommy Paul, and Arthur Fery over Taylor Fritz
 Semifinals : Berrettini over Vacherot and Humbert over Fery
 Final : Humbert over Berrettini

 European Open 
 Where : Brussels, Belgium  
 Surface : Indoor hard  
 Prize money : 723,435 Euros  
 Points : 250  
 Top seed : Arthur Fils
 2025 champion : Felix Auger-Aliassime (not playing)
 Draw analysis : Fils, who is trying to secure his Nitto ATP Finals spot, is the clear favorite in Brussels. However, the Frenchman’s path to the title is far from straightforward. He will open against Jaume Munar in round two before possibly running into Alex Michelsen in the quarterfinals and likely one of Belgium’s own in the semis — either Alexander Blockx or Zizou Bergs. The latter upset Carlos Alcaraz in Shanghai, so Bergs is brimming with confidence. Jiri Lehecka, Francisco Cerundolo, and Botic van de Zandschulp could be factors on the other side of the bracket.
 Hot : Jiri Lehecka, Alex Michelsen, Zizou Bergs, Botic van de Zandschulp, Juan Manuel Cerundolo
 Cold : Raphael Collignon, Tallon Griekspoor, David Goffin, Marcos Giron

 Semifinals : Bergs over Michelsen and Van de Zandschulp over Lehecka

 Almaty Open 
 Where : Almaty, Kazakhstan 
 Surface : Indoor hard  
 Prize money : $1,075,160
 Points : 250 
 Top seed : Daniil Medvedev
 Defending champion : Daniil Medvedev
 Draw analysis : For a 250-point tournament, Almaty is stacked. Headlining the field are Medvedev, Bublik, Rublev, Tsitsipas, and Karen Khachanov. There is plenty of danger in the unseeded ranks, too, including Tomac Machac, Roman Safiullin, Terence Atmane, and Adrian Mannarino. Competing in the final event of his career, Kazakhstan’s Mikhail Kukushin has already advanced to the second round. The 38-year-old awaits either Tsitsipas or Aleksandar Kovacevic in his next match. Although upsets are certainly possible if not even probable, quarterfinal matchups could be Medvedev vs. Tomas Martin Etcheverry, Bublik vs. Khachanov, Rublev vs. Nikoloz Basilashvili, and Tsitsipas vs. Luciano Darderi.
 Hot : Daniil Medvedev, Karen Khachanov, Rei Sakamoto
 Cold : Andrey Rublev, Tomas Machac, Marin Cilic, Terence Atmane, Mikhail Kukushkin
 Quarterfinal predictions : Daniil Medvedev over Rinky Hijikata, Karen Khachanov over Alexander Bublik, Adrian Mannarino over Nikoloz Basilashvili, and Stefanos Tsitsipas over Luciano Darderi
 Semifinals : Medvedev over Khachanov and Tsitsipas over Mannarino
